top_choice_rationale: Anne Carson is the only writer on the slate, and I rank the proposal first on the strength of the writing rather than the unanimous support in the record. Her voice is recognisable within a few lines. Autobiography of Red turns the Geryon material into a verse novel, and Nox makes an elegy from translation, commentary and archival fragments, so the form carries the grief. Loss, desire, inheritance and the limits of translation recur across verse, essay, drama and versions from Greek, which reads as one exacting project. The citation should credit her original lyric, verse narrative and essay as the core, with translation counted where it is a method inside her own books, as in Nox, and with stand-alone translations and classical scholarship as context. It should also name the exposed feeling so that it cannot be read as a prize for erudition. The main uncertainties are maturity after Nox, since I cannot verify from public knowledge whether the later books deepen the project or refine a settled method. Further uncertainties are the dependence of some effects on typography and page design, uneven travel into Swedish, and the placement of the boundary between original work and scholarship. None of these outweighs the case for the core oeuvre, so a prize is preferable to no award. This rests on public knowledge of representative works, and I have not read or independently verified the texts.
